title: Onboarding & Cold-Start Review — run #4 (trend vs 2026-10-23): Jira team on its own runner
description:
## As asked

<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="onboarding-cold-start-review" -->
Operator note: Context, not scope: the first outside users will be a small team who already use agents, work in Jira, and run tasks on their own runner. Read the cold start as they would meet it.

**Periodical Stage-2 task.** Run the **Onboarding & Cold-Start Review** for Harbour (the `LinearViewer` repo, live at `https://harbour.cat`, plus its runner seam: the in-repo own-session runner kit and the `simple-dispatcher` repo), then hand it off. This review's evidence is a **performed cold-start journey**. You actually try to use the product from a standing start and record what happened at each step. Reading onboarding artifacts in the abstract does not count.

This is **run #4 of the series.** It trends against run #3, `docs/reviews/onboarding-cold-start-review-2026-10-23.md` (LIN-3791, PR #2043), which pinned `LinearViewer` `661124c1` and `simple-dispatcher` `bb1da78`. The specifics below were **discovered on 2026-11-11** at `LinearViewer` `origin/main` `da5df707d` (**480 commits** after `661124c1`) and `simple-dispatcher` `origin/main` `5d8489e` (**67 commits** after `bb1da78`). They are a starting point to re-ground against the live product and your own HEAD, not a checklist to stay inside.

---

## 1. Audit the scope before executing

Treat the scope below as a floor to extend. Before walking anything, look for cold-start surfaces that are **in the remit but not listed** here, and fold them in. A scope you could only shrink is suspect; the expected move is to widen it to what the remit actually reaches.

Stay **broad in discovery, bounded in output.** The widened scope changes only *what you examine*. The report stays uncapped and severity-ranked (a clean, near-empty result is a genuine outcome). What you write into area notes stays within their rules: an entry only where a finding binds a builder or waits in an area, each note under its byte cap. Breadth belongs in the search, not in padded output.

Ways to find unlisted surfaces: `git diff --name-only 661124c1..HEAD` mapped through `docs/areas/areas.json`; the route list in `routes/`; the sign-in doors in `lib/components/landing-hero.js` (`signInDoors()`); `/sitemap.xml`, `/robots.txt`, `/llms.txt`, `/getting-started.md` on the live site; and the persona in the operator note above.

## 2. Read prior runs first (this review is trend-aware)

Read all three earlier reports (`docs/reviews/onboarding-cold-start-review-2026-08-29.md`, `…-2026-09-26.md`, `…-2026-10-23.md`; confirm no later `onboarding-*` report landed first) and run #3's evidence transcript `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-10-23/onboarding-cold-start-walk.md`. Frame **every journey step as a delta against run #3**: new, unchanged, improved, worsened, or resolved. Never write a point-in-time snapshot. Reuse run #3's stable step names (J1–J11, R1, D1, v1) so the ledgers compare mechanically; add new names for new journeys.

Run #3's findings to re-test, with their tickets as of discovery:

* **R3-1** `scripts/env-check.sh` false macOS Playwright blocker and no non-zero `exit`: **LIN-2386** (Backlog). The script changed in this window, so re-run it, don't assume.
* **R3-2** Local workspaces not re-enterable from a new session or by email account: **LIN-3065**, **LIN-3141** (Backlog).
* **R3-3** GitHub Projects advertised, no linked entry: **LIN-2387** (Todo).
* **R3-4** Hosted email send ceiling silently refuses: **LIN-3789** is now **Done**. Verify resolved on the live product.
* **R3-5** Zero-credential self-host shows "Log in with Linear" that 503s: **LIN-3108** (Backlog).
* **R3-6** The best cold path (hosted Local → free-tier grounded prompt) is unadvertised. **LIN-4085 (Done)** added an agent onboarding prompt under the sign-in buttons and `/getting-started(.md)`; landing rework **LIN-3980/LIN-3995** also shipped. Judge whether this closes R3-6 by walking it.
* **R3-7** Guest share page `/t/:token` has no onward path (LIN-3369 Backlog). **R3-8** headless endpoints undocumented (**LIN-3058** Backlog). **R3-9** seeded welcome tasks read as real work (**LIN-3069** Backlog). **R3-10/R3-11** destination docs lag (`README.md` and `/llms.txt` line 3 still say "collapsible tree"). **R3-12–R3-15** low friction (`.env.example` OpenRouter warning, runner bootstrap hand-exchange, `simple-dispatcher` zero-config `ENOENT workspaces.json`, bare 404s on `/login` and `/docs`). **R3-16** destination not reached end-to-end cold. **R3-17** the `/kpis` funnel read (see §5 below on telemetry).

## 3. Pin the destination first

Before walking, discover the project's own stated purpose and freeze it as this run's destination: what "used as intended" means. Today it is stated in several places that disagree in breadth: `CLAUDE.md`'s opening ("a provider-agnostic control plane … reads any issue backend, generates grounded prompts, dispatches them to AI agents, and verifies the work on real evidence"), `README.md:3` (narrower "collapsible tree"), `docs/v1.md`, `docs/north-star.md`, and the served `/getting-started.md` ("reads the person's task tracker … writes a checked prompt … runs that prompt on a coding agent, and checks the result against evidence"). Pick and quote the authoritative one, record the others as divergences (D1), and freeze it. If purpose has changed since run #3's frozen destination, report that as a delta, never a silent redefinition. For this run's persona, "used as intended" concretely means: **a Jira-backed workspace, a task from it run on the team's own runner, and the result checked on evidence.**

## 4. Run the review

Declare a zero state (no `.env` from this dispatch workspace, a fresh cookie jar, fresh `git clone`s in a scratch directory, no Harbour knowledge beyond what each surface gives you). Then discover the distinct cold-start entry paths and, for each, attempt it step by step as a genuine first-timer. Record per step: **proceeded**, **had to guess** (worked only after trial and error or an inference the product didn't supply), or **hard-blocked** (no workaround). At the end of each journey, record whether the frozen destination was reached and how far.

Seed inventory (re-walk run #3's set, then add what this window and the operator's persona open):

* **J1–J11, R1, D1, v1** as in run #3 (hosted OAuth strip; advertised vs reachable backends; README-literal self-host; `npm run setup`/`env:check`; broker-delivered and standalone bootstrap; free-tier first action; pre-auth public surfaces; headless/local self-host; email magic link; own-session runner; guest share link; `simple-dispatcher` seam; destination divergence; the `docs/v1.md` promise steps).
* **J12 (new): agent-led onboarding.** The team already uses agents, so walk the path they are most likely to take: copy the prompt under the sign-in buttons on `/`, hand it to a coding agent, and follow `/getting-started.md` exactly as served (`routes/getting-started.js`, `lib/prompts/agent-onboarding.js`). Check each path it offers ends somewhere real, live and on a self-host (its `{{BASE_URL}}` must point at the self-host). Known open: **LIN-4090** (guide claims review), **LIN-4088** (door missing from the workspace-removal landing and `/swipe`).
* **J13 (new): Jira team.** Walk both Jira doors (API-token link and OAuth 3LO sign-in, per `README.md` "Jira Cloud (optional)") as far as you can without a Jira site, then mark the rest capability-gated. On a self-host with no Jira env vars, check the door degrades honestly (compare R3-5's Linear 503). Then, from source-free observation only, check what a Jira workspace meets downstream: `README.md` says creating new issues isn't supported on Jira, so walk whatever onboarding or first-run step would create an issue (`+ Add task`, follow-ups, a periodical mint) and record what a Jira user sees. Known open, for citation not re-filing: **LIN-4355** (As-asked block in Jira), **LIN-2008** (boards/sprints unmodelled), **LIN-2014** (scope selection on a large site), **LIN-2391** (docs misstate Jira).
* **J14 (new): the team's own runner.** Run controls now appear only for an owner with a live runner key or queue token (**LIN-3849**, Done). Walk, from a fresh workspace: how a newcomer learns a runner is needed, which runner the product points them to (the own-session runner kit via the Runner setup page, `routes/runner-setup.js` / `lib/runner-kit/`, versus `simple-dispatcher`), whether the two are told apart anywhere a newcomer reads, and how far each gets toward running a task (run #3 reached `poll → take` on self-host). Known open: **LIN-3989** (mixed "run on my machine ›" vs "Set up a runner" copy).
* **J15 (new): more than one person.** The persona is a small team. Discover whether a second person can join or see the same workspace (no invite route was obvious at discovery), what a non-owner can do, and whether runner copies (owner-only) block a teammate. Record what the product says, not what source implies.
* **Unowned seams** (in this review's scope because no sibling owns them): Jira parity on onboarding surfaces, and the cross-repo choice between the in-repo runner kit and `simple-dispatcher`.

The finding classes here (hard block, friction, reach, capability gate, divergence) are **examples, not a limit**. Discover the complete set for this remit from the repo; a class list is a floor, never a ceiling.

**Simulate first-time, log every reach.** Nothing actually stops you reading the checkout, prior reports, or `CLAUDE.md`; this is a discipline, not a sandbox. Attempt each step using only what that step's own surface offers (its copy, error messages, in-product prompts, and docs it explicitly links). Every time you reach for outside repo knowledge to get unstuck, log that as a finding in its own right (a **reach**), rather than silently using it.

**Separate hard blocks from friction; mark capability gates.** Keep hard blocks and friction distinct in the ledger. Where a step needs a browser, an email inbox, a Jira site, OAuth consent, or a human-held credential you don't have, mark it **capability-gated** and say so, rather than skipping or guessing. Remove any accounts or workspaces you create on the live site once the walk is done, and say that you did.

## 5. No funnel telemetry: do not assume it

Do not go looking for a signup/activation analytics signal or assume one is tracked. If none exists, say so plainly and continue with the performed walk as the primary signal. Run #3 recorded a public `/kpis` read as secondary corroboration (R3-17); carry that ledger row as "not re-measured" unless the walk itself crosses it, and never let it stand in for the walk. Any human feedback surface the product exposes is a secondary, capability-gated corroboration only.

## 6. Mind the altitude: do not double-flag

This review owns the **performed journey** from cold start to the frozen destination.

* Defer the *rendered* first experience (landing hero, empty states, CTA affordance, aesthetic verdict) to the **Design & Interface Review**. Report only how the journey behaved.
* Defer whether docs read well *in the abstract* to the **Documentation Review** (latest `docs/reviews/documentation-review-2026-11-10.md`). Report a doc only where following it failed mid-walk (a stale command, a broken link).
* Defer reading *code* cold to the **Comprehension-Debt Review**. This review never reads source to judge it; it walks the product as a user or agent would.
* Defer API contract quality to the **API Quality Review**, a live secret's handling to the **Security Review** (but route the secret itself to the person, below), and cross-review aggregation to **Integration & Surface Maturity** (latest `docs/reviews/integration-surface-maturity-review-2026-11-10.md`): feed it evidence, never duplicate its scorecard.

## 7. Write an uncapped, trend-framed report

Record it where the convention puts it: `docs/reviews/onboarding-cold-start-review-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`, with the step-by-step transcript in `docs/reviews/_evidence-<YYYY-MM-DD>/onboarding-cold-start-walk.md` (the pattern runs #1–#3 used; re-confirm before writing). The report is severity-ranked and uncapped: nothing, one thing, or many are all valid; don't pad or invent make-work. Ground each finding in the journey as walked this run, not in prior prose. Close with a compact **trend ledger**: each journey step under its stable name, with outcome, destination reached, severity, and delta vs 2026-10-23. If discovery genuinely turns up no such place, put the full report in this task's comment instead of inventing a location.

## 8. Feed the area notes; mint no follow-up tasks

Findings go into the repo's area notes, where the next change in an area reads them before it starts. This review creates no new tasks. Follow the notes' own rules, not assumptions here: the registry `docs/areas/areas.json` (first match wins; code paths only), the format and guard in `docs/areas/README.md`, the guard test `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` (6144-byte cap per note; first cited path must map to the note's area; cited paths must exist), and the one-home rule `LEFTOVER_RULE` in `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`. Several notes are near the cap at discovery (`agent-api.md` 6124 B, `llm-and-prompts.md` 6136 B, `runs-and-dispatch.md` 5916 B), so prune before you add.

* Start from what changed: list files changed between `661124c1` (run #3's pin) and HEAD, map each through the registry, and look first where work landed.
* In each note you touch, prune entries you find settled or no longer true, and distil it to stay under its cap.
* A finding that leaves work in an area gets a **Waiting** entry; a rule a builder there must follow gets a **Lesson**. Each entry cites the area's file first, then names its source as "Onboarding & Cold-Start Review, <the date of this run>", with this report as the second cited path.
* A finding already filed as a ticket (all the LIN- numbers in §2 and §4 among them, if still open) stays in the report only, never also in a note.
* `simple-dispatcher` has its own registry and notes (`simple-dispatcher/docs/areas/`). Where a finding binds only a `simple-dispatcher` file, follow that repo's rules in a companion docs-only PR touching only its notes, and post its URL beside the main one; otherwise keep it in the report and closing comment.
* Commit the report, its evidence file and the note edits together in **one docs-only pull request** on `LinearViewer` (convention: branch `docs/lin-<id>-onboarding-cold-start-review-<date>`, commits `docs(LIN-<id>): …`). Rebase it onto main and get it green under the notes guard and `ci-success`. Then hand off as §11 says: review approves it and close-out merges it, never this run.

**Route each finding that has no area note to the person, never to a ticket.**

* *A larger tidy* (a move bigger than a change should take on in passing): write it as a Waiting entry worded as a size of move, and also list it for the person in the closing comment.
* *A finding with no file in an area to cite* (dependency manifests and lockfiles, or urgent breakage such as a live secret): put it in the closing comment, addressed to the person.
* *A cross-area seam*: file it under the area a change would start from, naming the other side, and say plainly in the report that seams have no full home in the notes yet.
* *A repo with no area notes*: keep every finding in the report and closing comment only.

**Route objective breakage to the person, never to a ticket.** List each objective breakage (a broken or dead link, a documented command that doesn't exist or errors, a setup step that hard-blocks with no workaround, a 404/500 mid-journey) in the closing comment, ranked by severity; where it traces to a file in an area, also add it to that note as above. Friction (a step that needed guessing but eventually worked) never takes this route; it stays in the report's advisory tail.

## 9. Stay review-only

The report changes no code, config, or secrets, and no docs beyond the report, its evidence file, and the area-note edits. Running the project's own setup in a scratch clone or throwaway environment is inspection, not a change to ship; the repos under review are left untouched. An operator instruction to avoid touching files is about the code and docs *under review*; it does not override this task's deliverable.

## 10. Get a fresh-context adversarial second-read (required, structural)

After the report and note edits are written and before the hand-off, a genuinely separate reader answers one question cold: *"what is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"* **Tier 1 (preferred):** a wholly separate session with no memory of this run. **Tier 2 (accepted fallback):** a fresh-context sub-agent with no memory of the report-writing turn. **Tier 3** (this session re-reading its own report) **is not accepted.** State which tier you used.

Then post **one comment** on this task containing, together in a single body:

* `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE` or `Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE`
* `Differed from top finding: YES` or `Differed from top finding: NO` (whether the reader's answer differed from the report's top-ranked finding, independent of the verdict)
* `Disposition: fixed in place`, `Disposition: escalated`, or `Disposition: no change`

The engine reads that comment and refuses Done until all three are present in one body. Copy the same three fields, the tier, the question and the reader's full answer into a `## Adversarial Second-Read` section of the report. AGREE and DISAGREE both end in the normal hand-off; a DISAGREE is itself the escalation, never a reason to hold the hand-off.

## 11. Hand off: don't stop silently, and don't merge or set Done

* As soon as the area-notes PR is open, post its **full URL** as a comment on this task (the engine needs it before Done).
* Once the §10 second-read comment is posted, post a **closing comment**: a concise, severity-ranked summary with a link to the full report; the PR named; every objective breakage, larger tidy and no-area finding listed for the person; and who finishes (review approves, then close-out merges the PR, sets this task to Done, and posts the final summary).
* This run neither merges nor moves the task to Done; it stays In Progress until close-out finishes. Leave the PR rebased and green. If it genuinely can't be made green (required checks red, a conflict you can't resolve), name the blocker in the closing comment instead. Escalating, by DISAGREE or a named blocker, never blocks the hand-off.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** Delivers the run #4 cold-start review as asked: report, evidence walk, pruned area notes and second-read in one docs-only PR; no Survey or area-note finding binds on it, so nothing larger pays.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Close-out stub (run 4 research, 11 Nov)

Implemented as asked, with no deviations from the brief: the run #4 Onboarding & Cold-Start Review report, its evidence transcript, and area-note Waiting entries, docs only.

* LinearViewer PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2395](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2395>), merged as `fe2f1f0cb0a3e5857afab871b60e3552cc0802c3`.
* simple-dispatcher PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/336](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/336>), merged as `7d6c5c6704174ca0d243e78c8dda687c972019c9`.
* One post-approval fix (R4-5 reclassified from objective to friction, `b5758ac96`).
* One follow-up filed: LIN-4419 (Node engines pin, R4-16).

The findings summary, per-journey detail and second-read notes are in the report; the full pre-prune description is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

comments.body:
Area-notes PR for this Onboarding & Cold-Start Review (run 4): https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2395

Docs only: the report `docs/reviews/onboarding-cold-start-review-2026-11-11.md`, its evidence transcript, and four Waiting entries in `docs/areas/front-end-browser.md` and `docs/areas/front-end-pages.md`. A companion simple-dispatcher notes PR follows.

## Adversarial second-read (Tier 2: fresh-context sub-agent)

The reader got only these, and was not told the ranking or this session's notes:
- the report and evidence paths;
- run #3's report path;
- both repos and their windows (`661124c1..da5df707d`, `bb1da78..5d8489e`);
- the persona;
- the question, *"What is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"*

It worked read-only.

**Its answer.** J15 marked "does a second Jira teammate join the same workspace" as capability-gated, but source answers it:
- A Jira sign-in's workspace is keyed on the person: `jira:${accountId}` (`routes/jira-auth.js:745-771`). GitHub is keyed the same way; only Linear is keyed on the organisation (`routes/auth.js:210`).
- So each teammate who presses "Continue with Jira" gets a separate workspace over the same site, with its own owner, run controls and runner key. Nothing joins them or says so.
- Settings' "member" copy cannot hold there, and two teammates' runners could take the same issue unseen.
- For this persona that outranks the door and naming seams.

Lesser points:
- Jira implements none of the proxy reads, so an agent's `GET /issues` 422s (LIN-2816).
- LIN-4352 and LIN-4370 give Jira tasks a different first step than Local.
- R4-8's periodical wording was off.
- LIN-796 (`simple-dispatcher`) wasn't mentioned.
- The spot-checked citations held.

**What I did.** I verified every point at source and fixed them all in place (commit `d58694ac5` on PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2395):
- R4-11 is rewritten as a source-confirmed divergence and raised to **Med-High, the largest finding for this persona**. It has a Waiting entry in `docs/areas/auth-accounts-and-workspaces.md` and is listed for the person.
- J13 and R4-8 now carry the proxy-read 422s and the Jira first-step difference.
- J14 names LIN-796.

R4-1 (`env-check.sh`, LIN-2386) stays the top *objective* defect. No task is minted.

Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE
Differed from top finding: YES
Disposition: fixed in place

## LIN-4413 research notes: how run #4 walked it (11 Nov)

**Pins.**
- `LinearViewer` `da5df707d`, 480 commits after run #3's `661124c1`. The live footer `da5df70` is the same commit.
- `simple-dispatcher` `5d8489e`, 67 commits after `bb1da78`.

**Re-grounding.** None of the files the ticket references changed after it was created (21:24Z). `git log --since` over `scripts/env-check.sh`, `routes/getting-started.js`, `lib/prompts/agent-onboarding.js`, `lib/components/landing-hero.js`, `routes/runner-setup.js` and `README.md` is empty. The brief's premises held, with two refinements found by the walk:
- `README.md:3` and `/llms.txt:3` still say "collapsible tree", but `/llms.txt` now has a "Getting started" section.
- `docs/v1.md:107` is no longer stale.

**Scope, widened by search.**
- `git diff --name-only 661124c1..HEAD`, mapped through `docs/areas/areas.json`.
- 18 added route files. Only `routes/getting-started.js` is cold-reachable; the rest are session- or token-gated, including the one with a runtime-built path, `proxy-model-routing`.
- `signInDoors()`, now the one door list for both the hero and the guide.
- A 163-URL sweep of the sitemap, public-page hrefs and guide URLs. No dead links.
- New journeys J12–J15 from the persona.

**What I ran.**
- *Live.* One anonymous Local workspace, walked as a person (Playwright for client-rendered controls):
  - add-source rows, both Jira doors, and a bogus-token link (honest error);
  - the Proxy page → agent prompt → exchange → `/instructions`;
  - "Write the prompt" on the free tier (823 ms);
  - settings, the runner and dispatch pages, and a share link viewed cold.

  The workspace was then removed; afterwards the owner gets 302, the share link 404 and the token 401.
- *Fresh clone, zero-credential self-host.*
  - README literally and the repo scripts (`env:check` still exits 0 with the false blocker);
  - Linear doors, now four including the guide, all 503 with a branded page;
  - Jira OAuth gives an honest 503; the API-token door works with zero config but is not in the switcher;
  - the runner kit: `kit ok` → login → run controls appear → Run to PR → poll → **take** → broker → feedback (no subagent);
  - **Next step** 503s and spins forever when there is no AI.
- *Fresh clone, test mode.* The fake-Jira harness (logged as a reach) gives create 422, `+ Add task` to Jira's own dialog, and a periodical mint accepted.
- *Fresh clone, console email.* Twelve sends: 10 delivered, then an honest per-IP 429. The R3-4 global ceiling is gone.
- *`simple-dispatcher`.* Zero-config still exits with `ENOENT workspaces.json`.

**Per-layer audit.** One brief per journey (J1–J15, R1, D1, v1), with sources cited and deltas against run #3, is in §3 of the report. The step-by-step evidence is in `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-11/onboarding-cold-start-walk.md`.

**Closing the set.** The search that could have surfaced a missed door was the unauthenticated lines of the 18 added route files plus the sweep. It found only `/getting-started`. The class would be wrong if a door is mounted by a runtime path that nothing links to. The second-read caught a different kind of miss: a persona question I marked gated that source answered (Jira workspaces are per person). It is fixed in place.

`Surface Assessment: [lands cleanly]`. The report is review-only: one docs-only PR plus a companion notes PR. It needs no refactor.

Report and notes: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2395 · `simple-dispatcher` notes: https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/336

## Hand-off: LIN-4413, Onboarding & Cold-Start Review run 4

**Report:** `docs/reviews/onboarding-cold-start-review-2026-11-11.md`, in **PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2395**.
- The PR is docs only: the report, the evidence transcript, and Waiting entries in three area notes.
- It is rebased on main. Head `d58694ac5`: `ci-success` passed, as did Unit, E2E 1–4 and the secret scan.

**Companion:** https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/336. It adds `docs/areas/loop-and-routing.md`, docs only; unit tests passed.

**Findings, by severity:**
1. **R4-1 High, objective:** `env-check.sh` reports a false macOS Playwright blocker and exits 0 (LIN-2386). This is the fourth run in a row.
2. **R4-11 Med-High, the largest finding for this persona:** Jira and GitHub workspaces are per person, so a team pressing "Continue with Jira" splits into one workspace each, with nothing saying so. There is no invite or join on any provider. Source-confirmed after the second-read.
3. **R4-3 Med-High, objective:** Local workspaces cannot be re-entered (LIN-3065, LIN-3141).
4. **R4-2 Med, objective, new:** on a self-host without AI, Next step 503s and the spinner never stops.
5. **R4-6 Med:** the Jira API-token door is only in Settings › Sources; the switcher's `+ Jira` is OAuth only.
6. **R4-9 Med:** the choice between the runner kit and Simple Dispatcher is never presented. This is a cross-repo seam; seams have no full home in the notes yet.
7. **R4-8 Med:** through the proxy, Jira reads 422 (LIN-2816), and the create 422 goes undocumented (LIN-3807).
8. Lesser: R4-4/5/7 and R4-12 to R4-21.

**Improved since run 3:**
- R3-4 resolved (the email ceiling is gone).
- R3-6 largely closed: the agent guide, the `llms.txt` way in, and the free tier from the real button in 0.8 s live.
- `docs/v1.md` fixed.
- GitHub Projects is addable in-workspace.
- The runner reached take plus a live broker on a self-host.

**For the person:**
- *Objective breakage, ranked:* R4-1 (LIN-2386); R4-3 (LIN-3065); **R4-2** (un-ticketed, in the front-end-browser note); R4-4 (a zero-credential self-host offers Linear in four places, including `/getting-started.md`, and all 503: LIN-3108); R4-5 (LIN-2387).

- *No area home:*
